addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

# Todo

This file uses [Prose form](AGENTS.md#prose-form). It
contains near term tasks with a short description and
uses links or reference links for more details.

## In Progress

When a `## Todo` item is picked up, its text moves here: the
problem overview and its list of things to do. That is followed
by the "plan" — a bullet + sub-bullets list of the development
"ladder". Each step starts with a `[[N]]` reference slot —
replaced with the step's commit ref on first backfill, once
the step is pushed — then the version, the title, and a
`(done|current)` marker as appropriate:
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-0 blah (current)
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-1 blah blah
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-2 blah blah blah
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y close-out and validation

At close-out the ladder lives on as the cycle's chores
`### As-built ladder`, where the refs are preserved
(renumbered to that file's local `# References` slots).

## Todo

 Entries are in **strict priority rank** — #1 highest,
 descending. Reprioritize by moving an entry, then
 `vc-x1 fix-todo --no-dry-run TODO.md` to renumber.
 The numbers are positional rank, not stable IDs — to refer
 to a Todo, name it by its **title** (a greppable mention;
 a numbered list item has no anchor to link to), not its
 number. Long-tail entries
 live in [todo-backlog.md](notes/todo-backlog.md). Use the
 [Prose Form in AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#prose-form); deeper
 detail goes in `notes/chores/chores-NN.md` design
 subsections (link via `[N]` ref).

## Done

Completed tasks are moved from `## Todo` to here, `## Done`, as they are completed
and older `## Done` sections are moved to [done.md](notes/done.md) to keep this file small.

**Verified claims**

- **AGENTS.md byte-identity restored** — I diffed vc-x1's AGENTS.md against ours: identical. cycle-protocol.md is also still identical, so the shared-doc pair is clean between vc-x1 and this template. (iiac-perf, zc-msg-x1, tprobe still diverge, correctly left to Todos 19/20.)

**Things worth discussing**

1. **The README change is the most substantive part.** The rename broke the `<CODE>.claude` sibling default for the real templates — `vc-x1-bot-repo-template` is not `vc-x1-work-repo-template.claude` — so the example now passes an explicit `CODE,BOT` pair, with a generic `../tmpl` example keeping the default documented. That's a fair fix, but it means the rename traded a one-arg invocation for a two-name one. Backlog entry 32 (single template repo with `.claude/` as a subdir) would restore single-arg ergonomics; alternatively `init` could learn a second default mapping (`<X>-work-repo-template` → `<X>-bot-repo-template`). Worth deciding whether 32 makes that moot.
2. **A drive-by fix rode along**: chores-14.md was missing its `# References` header (the `[N]:` definitions sat bare after prose). The commit added it and did disclose it in the body — fine, just noting it wasn't part of the rename per se.
3. **TODO.md entries 19/20 were rewrapped, not just renamed.** The longer names forced a refill of those paragraphs to the 72-col width, which inflates the diff and buries the actual rename in rewrap noise. Content is unchanged otherwise. Minor: the commit body doesn't mention the rewrap.
4. **Two `Commits:` styles now coexist in chores-14** — the DRY-facade section uses `Commits: see [As-built ladder](#as-built-ladder)` (refs live on the rungs), the new section uses the plain empty `Commits:`. That's coherent — multi-commit cycle vs. single-commit section — but if the rung-carried style is becoming the norm for cycles, the conventions docs currently only describe the plain form.

content.text:
I checked the actual behavior, and it's sharper than the help text suggests: in dual mode `validate_templates` (init.rs:1148) validates **both** paths unconditionally. So today `--use-template ../vc-x1-work-repo-template` alone doesn't just "assume" a sibling — it **hard-errors** because `../vc-x1-work-repo-template.claude` doesn't exist. There is currently no way in dual mode to seed only the work repo and leave the bot repo bare. That directly conflicts with your actual usage (bot template sometimes absent).

Given that, I'd now drop my earlier name-mapping suggestion and go with removing the default entirely:

- **`CODE` alone → seed the work repo, bot repo starts bare.** No filesystem probing, no derived names. You get exactly what you passed.
- **`CODE,BOT` → seed both**, and a missing `BOT` still fails validation loudly — the explicit form keeps its error checking.

Why this beats the alternatives:

- **The mapping default (`-work-repo-template` → `-bot-repo-template`)** bakes one naming convention into the tool, and it still makes the bot template mandatory-by-default — which is backwards given the bot template is the optional half in practice.
- **An opportunistic default** ("use the sibling if it exists, else bare") is the worst of both: behavior silently changes based on what happens to sit next to the template directory. A stray or stale `foo.claude` sibling gets picked up with no signal; a typo'd one is silently skipped.
- The old `<CODE>.claude` default was only ever saving one argument, and after the rename it no longer matches the real repos anyway — the README already had to switch its example to the explicit pair. A default nobody's layout satisfies is just a trap.

Mechanically it's a small change: `parse_use_template` returns `(PathBuf, Option<PathBuf>)`, the dual branch validates bot only when present, and `prepare_local_repo` already accepts `Option<&Path>` for the template (the single-repo path uses that today), so the seeding side barely moves. Doc comment, README examples, and the `parse_use_template` tests are the rest.

It also composes cleanly with backlog 32 (single template repo with `.claude/` as a subdir): if that lands, `CODE` alone naturally seeds both sides from the one tree, and `,BOT` remains as the override for split layouts — or gets retired. Nothing about removing the default now paints you into a corner there.

The plain version: right now, leaving out the bot template doesn't skip it — vc-x1 invents a name and fails when it's not there. Since you often genuinely have no bot template, the fix is to make "not passed" mean "not used," and keep templates purely explicit.

content.text:
Makes sense — leaving it is a fine call. The default isn't *wrong*, it just doesn't match the current template names, and since you're mid-refactor on vc-x1 there's no point locking a decision now that the `.bot` rename will reopen anyway.

One thing worth flagging early for that future `.bot` rename, since it's bigger than a string sweep:

- **The mechanical surface** is wide but tractable: `parse_use_template`'s `.claude` concat, init's `session_dir = project_dir.join(".claude")`, the `/.claude` gitignore entry and `clean_exclude`, `.vc-config.toml`'s `path = "/.claude"`, the `<name>.claude` GitHub repo naming, and the whole shared doc set (AGENTS.md, cycle-protocol.md — family-wide, so it's a coordinated sync like the other shared-doc Todos).
- **Old ochid trailers are the durable part**: every published commit carries `ochid: /.claude/<chid>` paths. Those are immutable history, so resolution needs to keep understanding `/.claude` forever (or map it via `.vc-config.toml`) even after new commits write `/.bot`.
- **The `.claude` directory is also Claude Code's own project directory** — settings, skills, hooks live in `<project>/.claude/`, and the harness reads them from that literal path. Today the bot repo and the harness directory are the same thing, which is part of the design's economy. We think renaming the bot repo to `.bot` splits them: session data and project settings would live in two places, or `.claude` becomes a symlink into `.bot`, or the settings stay in `.claude` outside the bot repo. That's the real design question in the rename, more than the renaming itself.

None of that argues against `.bot` — decoupling the bot repo's identity from one vendor's directory name is a reasonable motive — it just means the rename is a cycle with a design section, not a chore. Might be worth a one-liner in vc-x1's backlog so the intent is recorded next to entry 32 (single-template restructure), since the two would naturally land together.

    resolve in priority order: explicit env var (e.g.
    `VC_X1_TEST_TMPDIR`) → user config
    (`~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`) → local
    `.vc-config.toml` → `std::env::temp_dir()` fallback.

45. **`vc-x1` version-string ref resolution.** Today version
    strings (`0.58.0`, `0.58.0-3`) live in commit titles and
    `Cargo.toml` but aren't git refs, so
    `git diff 0.58.0^1 0.58.0` fails with "ambiguous
    argument". Auto-tagging at close-out clutters the tag
    namespace fast (one tag per cycle); a resolver is cleaner:
    - `vc-x1 sha <ref>` primitive: accepts version strings,
      standard git refs (pass-through), jj refs (chids, `@`)
      and outputs a SHA on stdout. Composable into
      `git diff $(vc-x1 sha X)^1 $(vc-x1 sha X)`.
    - `vc-x1 diff` / `vc-x1 log` thin wrappers that accept
      the version-string vocabulary and dispatch to git.
    - Cycle-relative aliases: `prev`, `cur`, `prev~1c` for
      "N cycles back along `--first-parent`".
    - `--first-parent` awareness: version refs resolve to
      the merge commit (bare `X.Y.Z`), so `0.58.0^1` walks
      first-parent to `0.57.0` naturally.

Last program stage on purpose — leans on facade-owns-

50. **Rename default bot repo dir `.claude` → `.bot`.**
    Decouple the bot repo's identity from one vendor's
    directory name. Mechanical surface: init's
    `join(".claude")`, the `<CODE>.claude` template default,
    `<name>.claude` GitHub repo naming, the `/.claude`
    gitignore entry and clean_exclude, `.vc-config.toml`'s
    `path = "/.claude"`, and the shared doc set (family-wide
    sync).
    - Published ochid trailers (`ochid: /.claude/<chid>`)
      are immutable history — resolution must keep
      understanding `/.claude` (or map it via
      `.vc-config.toml`) even after new commits write
      `/.bot`.
    - `<project>/.claude/` is also Claude Code's own project
      dir (settings, skills, hooks are read from that
      literal path). We think the rename splits the bot repo
      from the harness dir: settings stay in a `.claude`
      outside the bot repo, or `.claude` symlinks into
      `.bot` — this is the real design question, more than
      the renaming itself.
    - Naturally lands with "Restructure templates" — one
      layout change for init/clone instead of two.

content.text:
Your reasoning holds up, and I'd sharpen it: the "historical records keep the old name" convention protects *records* — and a template's files aren't records, they're **seed material**. `init` copies the non-hidden tree into every new project, so any old-name mention here doesn't just sit in history, it *propagates* into every future repo seeded from the template. That flips the default: in vc-x1, old names in chores are immutable truth; here, they're a defect in the product.

Walking the three hit sites through that lens:

- **`.claude/README.md`** — unambiguous, fix regardless of stance: `# vc-x1-bot-repo-template` title, link to `vc-x1-work-repo-template`.
- **`notes/chores/chores-01.md`** — the narrative mention ("byte-for-byte across vc-template-x1, vc-x1, and iiac-perf") updates to the new name, and the two commit-ref URLs can point at `github.com/winksaville/vc-x1-work-repo-template/commit/...` — the 40-hex SHAs in the title slots don't change, so nothing is falsified; the URL is just a locator and GitHub redirects both forms. One wrinkle worth noting: this file is *also* the template's own live chores file (it records real commits of this repo, including `a680ff8` in our recent log), so it has a dual nature — seed content and working record at once. Updating names doesn't damage the record; the SHAs are the anchors.
- **`notes/jj-tips.md`** — the only genuinely tangled one. The old names live in captured shell transcripts, and the file is byte-identical shared-doc with vc-x1, which just decided (in the rename commit) to keep them as historical. Sweeping only here breaks byte-identity; but for a tips doc the transcripts are teaching examples, not evidence — rewriting the cwd in a prompt string doesn't falsify the jj behavior being demonstrated. So the clean options are: **(a)** sweep it in both repos — an uncommitted working-copy edit in vc-x1, per our never-commit rule, keeping identity intact; **(b)** sweep only here and accept the divergence until the next family sync; **(c)** leave jj-tips alone and scope "no old names" to the truly template-authored files.

My recommendation: do `.claude/README.md` and `chores-01.md` now — both are pure wins with no cross-repo entanglement — and pick (a) for jj-tips, since the edit is cosmetic, the byte-identity invariant is worth protecting, and vc-x1's "historical" call was made about *its* records, not about what the family's shared teaching doc should say. Which way do you want jj-tips handled?

  seeded for new Rust projects via `CargoRust.toml`.

  scratch harness that validated the sub-cycle squash recipes.
  Recover it from its introducing commit [[1]]:
  `git show bd2902617c2f:notes/substep-test.sh`.

Commits:

The shared protocol doc set — `AGENTS.md`,
`notes/cycle-protocol.md`, `notes/jj-tips.md` — now matches
byte-for-byte across vc-x1-work-repo-template, vc-x1, and

template takes the four review fixes agreed across the three
sessions; the adopters replaced their older copies wholesale, so

158	## Why `jj log` shows fewer commits than `gitk`
159	
160	If you're coming from git, jj's log output can be surprising compared to
161	tools like `gitk --all`.
162	
163	jj tracks *changes* (identified by change IDs), not individual git commits.
164	When you rewrite a change (`jj describe`, `jj rebase`, `jj squash`, etc.),
165	jj creates a new git commit and keeps the old one under `refs/jj/keep/*` as
166	undo history. `gitk --all` sees all of these obsolete commits; `jj log` only
167	shows the current version of each change.
168	
169	## Useful commands
170	
171	| Command | Description |
172	|---------|-------------|
173	| `jj log` | Show recent visible commits (default revset) |
174	| `jj log -r ::@` | Show **all** ancestors of the working copy |
175	| `jj log -r 'all()'` | Show all non-hidden commits (needed if you have multiple heads/branches) |
176	| `jj st` | Show the status of the Working and Parent commits |
177	| `jj st -r <chid>` | Status of the commit, `<chid>` such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |
178	| `jj show` | Show the Working commit (`-r @`) |
179	| `jj show -r <chid>` | Show the commit, `<chid>` such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |
180	| `jj evolog -r <chid>` | Show the evolution history of a single change |
181	| `jj op log` | Show operation history (each rewrite operation) |
182	
183	
184	In a single-branch workflow, `jj log -r ::@` and `jj log -r 'all()'` give
185	the same result. Use `all()` when you have multiple branches or heads.
186	
187	## Revsets
188	
189	Revsets (sets of revisions) are how jj addresses commits. A
190	revision is identified by `@`, a chid, or a cid, and revsets are
191	built from those identifiers plus the operators `-`, `+`, `..`,
192	and `::`. There is a complete language available — see
193	`jj help -k revsets`.
194	
195	Summary:
196	
197	- A revision (rev) is used for addressing/referring to commits.
198	- jj supports a change_id (chid) and commit_id (cid).
199	  - The chid is permanent and doesn't change.
200	  - The cid is the SHA of the current commit and changes with any
201	    change to it or its ancestors.
202	- A revset is a set of revisions.
203	- In many jj commands revsets can address multiple commits.
204	- There is one root commit; chid=zzz sha=0 owner=root.
205	- The root commit never has content nor description.
206	- There can be multiple independent lineages of commits off root():
207	  - to create:
208	    - `jj new 'root()'`
209	    - `git switch --orphan <name>`
210	  - to see these:
211	    - `jj log -r 'roots(~root())'`
212	    - `git log --all --max-parents=0 --oneline`
213	
214	The examples below show these primitives in action.
215	
216	### A jj repo with some commits
217	
218	Some examples of revisions/rev:
219	   - @, chid=tkpvsrop, cid=ad2ba9b4 is the current commit
220	   - @-, chid=wxtmosqz, cid=35ac2422 is the ancestor of the current commit
221	   - @--, chid=vktlnyvm, cid=a0b0285e is the ancestor of the ancestor and so on
222	
223	```
224	$ jj log -r 'all()'
225	@  tkpvsrop wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 ad2ba9b4
226	│  count 3
227	○  wxtmosqz wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 35ac2422
228	│  count 2
229	○  vktlnyvm wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 a0b0285e
230	│  count 1
231	○  nvwytkrw wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 base 54fd18f7
232	│  count 0
233	◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000
234	```
235	
236	Move @ to vktlnyvm. (This could also have been done with `jj edit -r @--`.)
237	
238	```
239	$ jj edit -r vkt
240	Working copy  (@) now at: vktlnyvm a0b0285e count 1
241	Parent commit (@-)      : nvwytkrw 54fd18f7 base | count 0
242	```
243	
244	### Referencing commits with relative revsets
245	
246	```
247	$ jj log -r @
248	@  vktlnyvm count 1
249	$ jj log -r @-
250	○  nvwytkrw base | count 0
251	$ jj log -r @--
252	◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000
253	$ jj log -r @+
254	○  wxtmosqz count 2
255	$ jj log -r @++
256	○  tkpvsrop count 3
257	$ jj log -r @+++      # empty — nothing that far out
258	$ jj log -r @---      # empty
259	$ jj log -r @..
260	○  tkpvsrop count 3
261	○  wxtmosqz count 2
262	$ jj log -r @::
263	○  tkpvsrop count 3
264	○  wxtmosqz count 2
265	@  vktlnyvm count 1
266	$ jj log -r ..@
267	@  vktlnyvm count 1
268	○  nvwytkrw base | count 0
269	$ jj log -r ::@
270	@  vktlnyvm count 1
271	○  nvwytkrw base | count 0
272	◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000
273	```
274	
275	#### Interpretation
276	
277	- `@-` and `@--` resolve to single revisions: parent and
278	  grandparent of @. `@+` and `@++` are children. The blank output
279	  for `@+++` and `@---` is the empty revset — there is no revision
280	  that far away in this chain.
281	- `@..` and `@::` are ranges going outward from @ toward
282	  descendants:
283	  - `@..` is the *open* form: descendants of @, **excluding** @
284	    itself (here: count 2 and count 3).
285	  - `@::` is the *closed* form: descendants of @, **including** @
286	    itself (here: @=count 1, count 2, count 3).
287	- `..@` and `::@` are ranges going inward from some implicit start
288	  toward ancestors of @:
289	  - `..@` includes @ and its ancestors but **excludes** the root
290	    commit (here: @=count 1, base=count 0).
291	  - `::@` includes the root commit as well.
292	
293	Mnemonic: `..` and `::` both produce ranges; `::` includes the
294	implicit endpoint (root or visible heads), `..` excludes it. The
295	named operand is always part of the result on the target side; on
296	the source side it depends on which dot-form is used (excluded by
297	`..`, included by `::`).
298	
299	### Referencing commits with absolute revsets
300	
301	```
302	$ jj log -r v          # unambiguous prefix of vktlnyvm
303	@  vktlnyvm count 1
304	$ jj log -r vktln
305	@  vktlnyvm count 1
306	$ jj log -r w+         # w matches wxtmosqz, + takes its child
307	○  tkpvsrop count 3
308	$ jj log -r w--
309	○  nvwytkrw base | count 0
310	$ jj log -r w..
311	○  tkpvsrop count 3
312	$ jj log -r ..w
313	○  wxtmosqz count 2
314	@  vktlnyvm count 1
315	○  nvwytkrw base | count 0
316	$ jj log -r w::
317	○  tkpvsrop count 3
318	○  wxtmosqz count 2
319	$ jj log -r ::w
320	○  wxtmosqz count 2
321	@  vktlnyvm count 1
322	○  nvwytkrw base | count 0
323	◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000
324	```
325	
326	#### Interpretation
327	
328	- `v` and `vktln` both resolve to chid `vktlnyvm` because they are
329	  unambiguous prefixes within this repo — no other chid starts
330	  with those letters.
331	- `w+` resolves in two stages: `w` matches `wxtmosqz` (count 2) by
332	  prefix, then `+` takes its child, giving count 3.
333	- `w--` grandparent of w.
334	- `w..` descendants of w, excluding w.
335	- `..w` ancestors of w, not including root.
336	- `::w` ancestors of w, including root.
337	- `w::` descendants of w, including w.
338	
339	Prefix rule: jj rejects ambiguous prefixes. If two chids both
340	start with the same letters, the prefix must be lengthened until
341	exactly one chid matches.
342	
343	## Cross-repo Linking with Git Trailers
344	
345	Each commit cross-references its counterpart in the other repo
346	via an `ochid:` git trailer. That is a cross-repo convention
347	rather than a jj mechanic — for the full definition (trailer
348	syntax, per-commit mechanics, `.vc-config.toml`) see
349	[Cross-repo linking (ochid trailers)](../AGENTS.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)
350	in AGENTS.md.
351

## Why `jj log` shows fewer commits than `gitk`

If you're coming from git, jj's log output can be surprising compared to
tools like `gitk --all`.

jj tracks *changes* (identified by change IDs), not individual git commits.
When you rewrite a change (`jj describe`, `jj rebase`, `jj squash`, etc.),
jj creates a new git commit and keeps the old one under `refs/jj/keep/*` as
undo history. `gitk --all` sees all of these obsolete commits; `jj log` only
shows the current version of each change.

## Useful commands

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `jj log` | Show recent visible commits (default revset) |
| `jj log -r ::@` | Show **all** ancestors of the working copy |
| `jj log -r 'all()'` | Show all non-hidden commits (needed if you have multiple heads/branches) |
| `jj st` | Show the status of the Working and Parent commits |
| `jj st -r <chid>` | Status of the commit, `<chid>` such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |
| `jj show` | Show the Working commit (`-r @`) |
| `jj show -r <chid>` | Show the commit, `<chid>` such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |
| `jj evolog -r <chid>` | Show the evolution history of a single change |
| `jj op log` | Show operation history (each rewrite operation) |


In a single-branch workflow, `jj log -r ::@` and `jj log -r 'all()'` give
the same result. Use `all()` when you have multiple branches or heads.

## Revsets

Revsets (sets of revisions) are how jj addresses commits. A
revision is identified by `@`, a chid, or a cid, and revsets are
built from those identifiers plus the operators `-`, `+`, `..`,
and `::`. There is a complete language available — see
`jj help -k revsets`.

Summary:

- A revision (rev) is used for addressing/referring to commits.
- jj supports a change_id (chid) and commit_id (cid).
  - The chid is permanent and doesn't change.
  - The cid is the SHA of the current commit and changes with any
    change to it or its ancestors.
- A revset is a set of revisions.
- In many jj commands revsets can address multiple commits.
- There is one root commit; chid=zzz sha=0 owner=root.
- The root commit never has content nor description.
- There can be multiple independent lineages of commits off root():
  - to create:
    - `jj new 'root()'`
    - `git switch --orphan <name>`
  - to see these:
    - `jj log -r 'roots(~root())'`
    - `git log --all --max-parents=0 --oneline`

The examples below show these primitives in action.

### A jj repo with some commits

Some examples of revisions/rev:
   - @, chid=tkpvsrop, cid=ad2ba9b4 is the current commit
   - @-, chid=wxtmosqz, cid=35ac2422 is the ancestor of the current commit
   - @--, chid=vktlnyvm, cid=a0b0285e is the ancestor of the ancestor and so on

```
$ jj log -r 'all()'
@  tkpvsrop wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 ad2ba9b4
│  count 3
○  wxtmosqz wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 35ac2422
│  count 2
○  vktlnyvm wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 a0b0285e
│  count 1
○  nvwytkrw wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 base 54fd18f7
│  count 0
◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000
```

Move @ to vktlnyvm. (This could also have been done with `jj edit -r @--`.)

```
$ jj edit -r vkt
Working copy  (@) now at: vktlnyvm a0b0285e count 1
Parent commit (@-)      : nvwytkrw 54fd18f7 base | count 0
```

### Referencing commits with relative revsets

```
$ jj log -r @
@  vktlnyvm count 1
$ jj log -r @-
○  nvwytkrw base | count 0
$ jj log -r @--
◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000
$ jj log -r @+
○  wxtmosqz count 2
$ jj log -r @++
○  tkpvsrop count 3
$ jj log -r @+++      # empty — nothing that far out
$ jj log -r @---      # empty
$ jj log -r @..
○  tkpvsrop count 3
○  wxtmosqz count 2
$ jj log -r @::
○  tkpvsrop count 3
○  wxtmosqz count 2
@  vktlnyvm count 1
$ jj log -r ..@
@  vktlnyvm count 1
○  nvwytkrw base | count 0
$ jj log -r ::@
@  vktlnyvm count 1
○  nvwytkrw base | count 0
◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000
```

#### Interpretation

- `@-` and `@--` resolve to single revisions: parent and
  grandparent of @. `@+` and `@++` are children. The blank output
  for `@+++` and `@---` is the empty revset — there is no revision
  that far away in this chain.
- `@..` and `@::` are ranges going outward from @ toward
  descendants:
  - `@..` is the *open* form: descendants of @, **excluding** @
    itself (here: count 2 and count 3).
  - `@::` is the *closed* form: descendants of @, **including** @
    itself (here: @=count 1, count 2, count 3).
- `..@` and `::@` are ranges going inward from some implicit start
  toward ancestors of @:
  - `..@` includes @ and its ancestors but **excludes** the root
    commit (here: @=count 1, base=count 0).
  - `::@` includes the root commit as well.

Mnemonic: `..` and `::` both produce ranges; `::` includes the
implicit endpoint (root or visible heads), `..` excludes it. The
named operand is always part of the result on the target side; on
the source side it depends on which dot-form is used (excluded by
`..`, included by `::`).

### Referencing commits with absolute revsets

```
$ jj log -r v          # unambiguous prefix of vktlnyvm
@  vktlnyvm count 1
$ jj log -r vktln
@  vktlnyvm count 1
$ jj log -r w+         # w matches wxtmosqz, + takes its child
○  tkpvsrop count 3
$ jj log -r w--
○  nvwytkrw base | count 0
$ jj log -r w..
○  tkpvsrop count 3
$ jj log -r ..w
○  wxtmosqz count 2
@  vktlnyvm count 1
○  nvwytkrw base | count 0
$ jj log -r w::
○  tkpvsrop count 3
○  wxtmosqz count 2
$ jj log -r ::w
○  wxtmosqz count 2
@  vktlnyvm count 1
○  nvwytkrw base | count 0
◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000
```

#### Interpretation

- `v` and `vktln` both resolve to chid `vktlnyvm` because they are
  unambiguous prefixes within this repo — no other chid starts
  with those letters.
- `w+` resolves in two stages: `w` matches `wxtmosqz` (count 2) by
  prefix, then `+` takes its child, giving count 3.
- `w--` grandparent of w.
- `w..` descendants of w, excluding w.
- `..w` ancestors of w, not including root.
- `::w` ancestors of w, including root.
- `w::` descendants of w, including w.

Prefix rule: jj rejects ambiguous prefixes. If two chids both
start with the same letters, the prefix must be lengthened until
exactly one chid matches.

## Cross-repo Linking with Git Trailers

Each commit cross-references its counterpart in the other repo
via an `ochid:` git trailer. That is a cross-repo convention
rather than a jj mechanic — for the full definition (trailer
syntax, per-commit mechanics, `.vc-config.toml`) see
[Cross-repo linking (ochid trailers)](../AGENTS.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)
in AGENTS.md.

content.text:
That quoted sentence is ambiguous because its two halves pull in opposite directions: "leave it identical" says the shared wording is fine, while "our .claude isn't the template" is precisely the reason the wording is *wrong*. Your fuller thought resolves the tension the right way — instead of deciding whether the README's claim is true, **make it true by design**.

And I think the design is sound. Here's how the pieces line up:

- **The bot seed is a fixed trio, not a tree.** What a new bot repo needs from a template is `LICENSE-*`, `README.md`, and the empty `memory/MEMORY.md` — static boilerplate. The current mechanism (recursive copy of arbitrary non-hidden contents) is a general tool doing a specific job. Teaching vc-x1 the manifest turns "whatever happens to be in the bot template" into a known contract.
- **A fixed manifest frees the source location.** Once init knows *what* to take, the trio can come from anywhere — including `<CODE>/.claude/` inside the work template. That's exactly backlog 32's single-template layout, and the manifest is what makes 32 clean: the code-side copy already skips hidden entries, so a `.claude/` subdir carrying the seed trio doesn't collide with it. The two ideas are really one design.
- **"We don't have a vc-x1-bot-repo-template"** — I read this as: under this design you wouldn't *need* one, and the separate repo gets retired. That also kills the sync burden that "identical" would otherwise create: today the trio would live in two places (the sibling repo and this `.claude`) and drift; with one source, identity is structural, not maintained.
- **The README claim heals itself.** With the sibling retired, this `.claude` (or the `.claude/` subdir) *is* the bot-side source, and "this repo is the source template for the bot side" becomes accurate — the live bot repo doubles as the living example. Init's existing first-line rewrite (`# <repo-name>`) already handles the one per-project difference.
- **One thing you'd give up**: the current generic copy lets a bot template ship anything. If that flexibility ever matters, the explicit `CODE,BOT` form can keep the generic-copy behavior while the manifest serves the default path. But given your earlier point — the bot template is the optional half anyway — I doubt you'll miss it.

For a later date, agreed — but it's worth a line in vc-x1's backlog next to entry 32 so the manifest idea and the retire-the-bot-template conclusion don't evaporate. Entry 32 could even absorb it ("single template; bot side seeds from a fixed manifest — LICENSE-*, README.md, empty memory/MEMORY.md — taken from `.claude/`"). Happy to amend it when you want.

The plain version: you're proposing that vc-x1 stop copying a whole second template and instead know the three things a new bot repo needs, taking them from inside the one template repo. That removes a repo, removes a sync problem, makes the README's self-description honest, and dovetails with the existing plan to merge the templates into one.

content.text:
That rule lands well — it's the classic explicit/implicit split: **if you pointed at something, you get all of it; if you didn't, the tool takes only what it knows it needs.** A few thoughts on how it plays out:

- **It quietly settles the default-bot-path debate too.** With "otherwise → fixed subset from inside the code template," the `<CODE>.claude` sibling derivation just disappears — there's no name to guess and no missing-sibling error. Explicit `,BOT` becomes the only path that can fail on a bad path, and it fails on something the user actually typed.
- **The subset is what makes seeding from a *live* `.claude` safe.** This workspace's `.claude` has non-hidden session artifacts at its top level (transcript `.jsonl` files and such). A generic non-hidden copy from it would drag session data into every new project — the fixed manifest (`LICENSE-*`, `README.md`, `memory/MEMORY.md`) is precisely the filter that lets the template's live bot repo double as the seed source without shipping its history. So the manifest isn't just convenience; it's the safety property.
- **Graceful degradation falls out naturally**: subset members that don't exist in the source just aren't seeded — init already generates the true minimum (`.vc-config.toml` etc.) itself, so a code template with no `.claude/` content yields a bare-but-valid bot repo, which matches your "bot template is optional" reality.
- **One possible refinement**: `memory/MEMORY.md` may not belong in the manifest at all. Its content is *nothing* — it exists only because Claude tends to create it otherwise. That's the profile of a generated file, not a copied one: init could emit the empty file alongside `.vc-config.toml`, shrinking the copied subset to `LICENSE-*` + `README.md` and removing the "is it still empty?" invariant from the template. The counterargument is visibility — a file in the template documents itself — but generation is one less thing to keep in sync.
- **Explicit mode stays the escape hatch** for anyone who genuinely wants a richer bot seed, and its semantics ("everything non-hidden, exactly like the code side") stay symmetric and easy to explain in `--help`.

The plain version: no argument means the tool copies only its short known list, so nothing surprising can leak in; giving an argument means you asked for that directory, so you get all of it. The one tweak I'd consider is having vc-x1 create the empty memory file itself rather than copying it.

When you're ready, this whole design (subset rule + retire the bot template + fold into the single-template restructure) belongs in vc-x1's backlog entry 32 — say the word and I'll rewrite that entry to absorb it.

      tends to create it otherwise), so init emits it like

No, you misinterpreted my statement. Here chores-01.md is never
recording history, this is a template, thus a starting point.
History is captured in this repo's commits and conversation not
in the body, thus there are no todo's and so forth. Make sense?

content.text:
Yes — that makes sense now, and it's a cleaner principle than the one I was arguing. Let me restate it to confirm:

- In **vc-x1**, chores files are a genuine historical record of shipped work — old names stay, content is immutable narrative.
- **Here**, nothing in a file body is a record. The template's history lives where history always lives — this repo's commits and the bot repo's conversations. Every tracked file body is *seed content*: the starting point a new project begins from. So chores-01.md should not contain the template's own past work at all — no real Done narrative, no `Commits:` backfills, no refs to actual template SHAs.

That reframes what happened with my sweep: I treated the symptom (old names inside a history section) when the actual defect is that the history section exists in a template file. The restore wasn't "keep the old names" — it was declining a pointless polish of content that shouldn't be there. The `vc-template-x1` mentions now sitting in chores-01.md are moot, because the sections containing them should go entirely.

The implication for this repo: chores-01.md gets reduced to a skeleton — an instructional intro showing the shape (like TODO.md here already is: structure and conventions demonstrated, empty of real entries) with its two real-history sections and their `[1]`/`[2]` commit refs removed. # Notes

This directory contains various notes and documentation related to the project.
Each file is organized by topic for easy reference.

By default there are chores/chores-*.md here, and the short-term task
list lives in the repo-root [`../TODO.md`](../TODO.md). Chores are general
notes about tasks and `../TODO.md` contains short term tasks and their status.
The chores-NN files are numbered in sequence; as a chores file grows
large the next one is opened ([chores/chores-01.md](chores/chores-01.md)
is the active one in this template), and earlier ones are closed and
kept for history.


Examples chore file:
```
# Chores-01.md
 
General maintenance tasks and considerations for the project see other files for
more specific topics. A chore in a chores file provides quick information on the
how and why of a particular chore.

## Create a binary that lists jj info 

This binary should list the changeID, commitID, and description title
and using `jj-lib`
```

## Workflow and conventions

Bot-facing workflow and conventions live in
[`../AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md):

- [Notes file conventions](../AGENTS.md#notes-file-conventions)
  — Todo format, Reference numbering, Notes references
  (`[[N]]` citation style), Markdown anchor links, Retiring
  Done entries.
- [Chores conventions](../AGENTS.md#chores-conventions) —
  section headers / Done entries exact-title rule, content
  rules, `Commits:` line format.
- [Code Conventions](../AGENTS.md#code-conventions) — doc
  comments, `// OK: …` on `unwrap*` calls, ask-on-ambiguity,
  stuck detection.

Per-cycle workflow lives in
[`cycle-protocol.md`](cycle-protocol.md):

- [Cycles](cycle-protocol.md#cycles) — three-phase shape
  (Preparation → Work → Close-out), `X.Y.Z-N` numbering,
  sub-cycles.
- [Per-commit flow](cycle-protocol.md#per-commit-flow) —
  cargo cycle (`fmt` / `clippy` / `test` / `install`),
  work + commit description review gates.
- [Commit description](cycle-protocol.md#commit-description)
  — Conventional Commits, no `(version)` suffix; body shape
  per work vs bot repo.
- [Pushing](cycle-protocol.md#pushing) — push policy,
  close-out shape, `.claude` cadence.

This repo's versioning lives in
[`versioning.md`](versioning.md) — generic and shared
verbatim; the single source of truth that AGENTS.md and
cycle-protocol.md refer to abstractly:

- [Terms](versioning.md#terms) — version / version-of-record /
  versioning.
- [Recording the version-of-record](versioning.md#recording-the-version-of-record)
  — manifest, notation, reporter, and cadence, by medium.
- [Step numbering](versioning.md#step-numbering) — the
  `X.Y.Z-N` scheme, nesting, optional Preparation.

235	
236	[Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/):
237	
238	```
239	<type>: <short description>
240	```
241	
242	Titles carry **no trailing `(<version>)` suffix**. The
243	version-of-record — where it lives and its bump cadence, see
244	[versioning.md](versioning.md) — is useful for confirming
245	you're running the version you're testing, not a per-commit
246	title marker. We think per-commit version-in-title is
247	unstable on large projects: many changes are in flight
248	simultaneously, and a
249	version is only stable once merged into the main repo — so
250	titles don't carry one.
251	
252	### Title
253	
254	- ≤50 chars total.
255	- Common types: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `test`,
256	  `docs`, `chore`.
257	- Favor terse phrasings.
258	- **Distinct per step** — each of a cycle's commits gets its
259	  own descriptive title (no shared cycle title with a step
260	  marker). Share a greppable stem across the cycle's titles
261	  (e.g. `ring buffer`) so `git log --grep` collects them; the
262	  chores section header matches the close-out title. See
263	  AGENTS.md
264	  [Conventional-commit shape](../AGENTS.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--chores--commit).
265	
266	### Body
267	
268	[Prose form](../AGENTS.md#prose-form) (intro + bullets),
269	wrap ≤72. Bullet content differs per repo:
270	
271	- **Work-repo body**: file-by-file. One bullet per file
272	  changed (file plus a one-line gist). Sub-bullets for
273	  files with multiple distinct changes:
274	
275	  ```
276	  - path/to/file1
277	    - first distinct change
278	    - second distinct change, wrapping to next line
279	       with continuation indented 5
280	  ```
281	
282	  The file-by-file list is the source of truth for the
283	  cycle's mechanical change record. Chores carries the
284	  narrative + design, not a copy of it. Promote any
285	  "why" beyond one sentence to a chores `###` subsection.
286	
287	- **Bot-repo (`.claude`) body**: bullets describe
288	  in-session activity rather than work-repo changes.
289	
290	### Trailer
291	
292	`ochid:` as the last line of the body — see
293	[Cross-repo linking (ochid trailers)](../AGENTS.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)
294	in AGENTS.md for the convention.
295	
296	For breaking changes, use the hyphenated `BREAKING-CHANGE:`
297	trailer key. `BREAKING CHANGE:` (with a space) is the only
298	space-separated key the Conventional Commits spec allows; the
299	hyphenated form is also valid and avoids the space ambiguity.
300	
301	## Reviewing changes
302	
303	Work review looks at the **uncommitted working-copy diff**,
304	on the way to commit. The user opens diffs in their
305	editor (Zed, VSCode); jj commands are for terminal:
306	
307	- `jj diff` — working-copy diff (uncommitted)
308	- `jj diff -r @-` — diff of the previous commit
309	- `jj diff --from <X> --to <Y>` — any two revisions
310	- `jj show -r <X>` — description + diff for one rev
311	
312	Don't `jj edit -r @-` to view a past commit — that marks
313	it mutable and shifts `@`; use `jj diff -r @-` or
314	`jj show -r @-`.
315	
316	See [Sub-cycle ladders](#sub-cycle-ladders) for the
317	close-out squash recipe and recovery; revset primitives
318	are in [`jj-tips.md`](jj-tips.md#revsets).
319	
320	## Pushing
321	
322	### Policy
323	
324	Push is **discretionary** during the cycle (backup,
325	progress visibility) and **mandatory at close-out** —
326	the cycle's result must be published.
327	
328	**Approval is per-push.** Every push — any repo, any kind:
329	cycle push, interim backup, recovery/surgery force-push —
330	happens only after the user has reviewed the changes to be
331	published and explicitly approved that specific push.
332	Approval of a plan that *includes* a push does not authorize
333	the push itself; stop and ask again at the moment of pushing.
334	
335	**Default is interactive; an explicit scoped delegation waives
336	the gates.** The gates above — per-push approval, the
337	commit-description review (show title+body and stop), and the
338	hard stop after push/squash-push — are the *interactive
339	default*.
340	They yield when the user **explicitly** delegates a complete,
341	bounded task and authorizes carrying it through ("do all of X
342	and push each step, don't check in"). The bot then proceeds
343	through that task's commits and pushes without stopping, and
344	continues past each push to the next step. Conditions:
345	
346	- **Explicit grant** — never inferred from a task merely being
347	  well-scoped; the user's words must authorize unattended
348	  completion. "Commit and push" (or "then push") names the
349	  destination, not a waiver: it authorizes the push *after*
350	  the normal work review and description review, not skipping
351	  them. Only wording that explicitly waives the stops ("don't
352	  check in", "no need to review", "carry it through
353	  unattended") waives them.
354	- **Bounded goal** — covers the named task only; does not carry
355	  to the next task or a vaguer follow-on.
356	- **Destructive ops still pause** — delegation covers the task's
357	  ordinary commits and pushes; it does *not* pre-authorize a
358	  genuinely irreversible action (force-push over published
359	  history, history rewrite, deleting a remote branch). Those can
360	  permanently destroy work and aren't a normal cycle step, so the
361	  bot flags one before acting. An ordinary delegated cycle never
362	  reaches this.
363	- **Still transparent** — report each commit/push as it lands

vc-x1 0.73.2

Commit both repos, push the work repo's BOOKMARK, and
squash-push the bot repo's `main` — one resumable command.

Collapses the manual commit-push-publish ceremony into a
single subcommand with two interactive approval gates and a
state machine with persistent progress so interruptions can
resume without re-doing completed stages.

Stages: preflight (tracking / bot-published / sync checks —
no build steps; run project checks yourself before pushing)
→ review (approve diff)
→ message ($EDITOR / --title+--body, approve text) →
commit-work → commit-bot (skipped if clean) → bookmark-set
(work repo → <bookmark>, bot repo → main) → push-work →
squash-push-bot. Failures in commit-work / commit-bot /
bookmark-set roll both repos back via
`jj op restore` to the snapshot recorded before commit-work.
After push-work succeeds the remote boundary is crossed and
recovery is forward-only.

Non-interactive use: pass both --title and --body plus --yes
to skip the review gate. Saved state carries title/body
across resumes so only the first invocation needs them.

Usage: vc-x1 push [OPTIONS] [BOOKMARK]

Arguments:
  [BOOKMARK]
          Bookmark to advance in the work repo (positional form of
          `--bookmark`). The bot repo always advances `main`.
          
          Accepting a positional lets the common case read as `vc-x1 push main`
          without the `--bookmark` ceremony; `--bookmark` is kept as an alias
          for scripts and for composition with other args. The two forms
          conflict if both supplied.

Options:
      --bookmark <BOOKMARK>
          Bookmark to advance in the work repo (flag form; see positional)

  -V, --version
          Print the `vc-x1 X.Y.Z` banner as the first line, then continue. With
          no subcommand, prints the banner and exits.
          
          Replaces clap's auto-version (which would exit after printing): the
          banner now rides along with normal subcommand execution rather than
          gating it, so scripts can capture the version *and* the command's
          output in one invocation.

      --restart
          Clear any saved state file and start from stage 1

  -v, --verbose...
          Verbose output: -v debug, -vv trace

      --from <STAGE>
          Explicit stage to jump to (advanced / debug use)

          Possible values:
          - preflight:       Verify bookmark tracking, the bot-published
            invariant, and sync state
          - review:          Present diff for the first approval gate
          - message:         Compose / edit the commit message; present for
            second gate
          - commit-work:     Commit the work repo
          - commit-bot:      Commit the `.claude` bot repo (skipped if empty)
          - bookmark-set:    Advance each repo's bookmark to its `@-`: work →
            `<bookmark>`, bot → `main`
          - push-work:       `jj git push --bookmark <b> -R .`
          - squash-push-bot: In-process squash of `.claude`'s trailing session
            writes + push `main`

      --log <LOG>
          Log file path (captures all levels)

      --step
          Pause between every stage for an interactive approval gate

      --status
          Print where the saved state thinks we are and exit

      --recheck
          Re-run `preflight` even on resume (default: skip if last run
          succeeded)

      --no-squash-push
          Stop before `squash-push-bot` so it can be run manually

      --dry-run
          Print the exact commands for every stage without side effects

      --title <STR>
          Commit title (skip `$EDITOR` for the message stage)

      --body <STR>
          Commit body (skip `$EDITOR` for the message stage)

  -y, --yes
          Auto-approve interactive prompts (review gate, message-edit
          confirmation). Required when `--title` / `--body` aren't both supplied
          in non-interactive contexts

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
